operations.name: join
operations.description:
Creates a new customer account by validating email uniqueness and storing a cryptographically hashed password. This operation confirms identity through email verification after creation. The registration flow requires the email and password_hash fields from the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon successful join, a session is initiated with access and refresh tokens issued via the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. This operation is required as the customer actor is a member type with full authentication capability and joins via credential-based registration.

The system MUST validate email uniqueness against the shopping_mall_customers.email field. Passwords are stored as hash in shopping_mall_customers.password_hash and must meet complexity requirements (design implied by schema). Registration creates a new customer record in shopping_mall_customers and an initial session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. The system must send an email verification token to the provided email, linked to shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications. No pre-authentication state is required; join is the entry point for unauthenticated users.

A successful join response returns an IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized object with a new access token (30-min TTL) and refresh token (30-day TTL), both mapped to the generated session record. Invalid registration (duplicate email, weak password) returns 422. The token generation mechanism relies on the JWT infrastructure supplied by authN service, binding to the customer.id.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the initial entry point for customer identity creation and does not rely on prior system state. All operations downstream depend on this being completed first. Subsequent operations (login, refresh) require this session state.
operations.specification: The service layer creates a new shopping_mall_customers record with email and password_hash. It generates a unique verification token, inserts it into shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications with 1-hour expiration, and generates a JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day). These are stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with customer_id linked. Session records include IP and referrer for audit. Response returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized with tokens. Validation checks: email format, uniqueness in shopping_mall_customers, password length/complexity. Upon failure, no record is created or token generated. Immutable session audit trail maintained.

requestBody.description: Request payload to create a new customer account with email and password.

responseBody.description: Response containing access and refresh JWT tokens and customer identifier post-registration.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Verifies customer credentials by matching submitted email and password against the stored hash in the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon successful authentication, generates a new JWT access token (30-min) and refresh token (30-day) and stores them in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation is required for all member actors to establish an authenticated session after registration. The customer actor type requires login to access protected resources.

The system validates the email exists in shopping_mall_customers and that the password_hash matches the submitted plaintext password after cryptographic hashing. If both validations pass, it generates new tokens and creates or updates a session record with client IP and referrer context. The operation fails with 401 if credentials mismatch, account is deleted (deleted_at not null), or if server-side technical errors occur.

The defined IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin body must contain email and password. The IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized response contains the new tokens and the customer ID associated with this login event. The refresh token enables token renewal without re-authenticating credentials.

This operation has no prerequisites as it is the primary entry point for authenticated sessions and does not require prior login or state. It is decoupled from pending email verification — residual verification tokens do not block login if the account exists and credentials are valid.
operations.specification: When login is called, server looks up customer in shopping_mall_customers by email. Checks if deleted_at is null. Computes hash of submitted password and compares to password_hash. On match, generates new JWTs: access token (30m) and refresh token (30d). Inserts new record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with IP, referrer, and expiry. Returns IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. On mismatch or account deleted, returns 401. Invalid input (missing email/password) returns 422. All token issuance is stateless and bound by customer_id. No session cleanup occurs on login—previous sessions remain valid unless manually revoked.

requestBody.description: Request containing email and plaintext password to authenticate customer and establish session.

responseBody.description: Response with newly generated access and refresh JWT tokens upon successful authentication.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Renews the access token by validating a previously issued refresh token stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. This operation allows the customer to maintain a session without re-entering credentials, reducing exposure to credential harvesting. The refresh token must be valid (not expired, not revoked) and associated with an active customer record. Both tokens persist in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table for audit and revocation tracking.

The system accepts a refresh token string and validates it against the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. If the token exists, its expired_at timestamp is later than current time, and the associated customer record has deleted_at = null, then a new access token is generated and returned. The refresh token itself is not renewed unless explicitly designed (per specification, it remains valid until expiration). This operation cements the stateless JWT architecture—no session persistence beyond token validity.

The IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh request body expects only the refresh token string. The response IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized returns a new access token with 30-minute TTL. The refresh token remains unchanged. If refresh token is invalid, expired, or belongs to a deleted customer, a 401 Unauthorized is returned.

This operation has no prerequisites. It can be called at any time if a valid refresh token exists, even without prior login during the session. It is the mechanism enabling stateless, long-duration authentication without re-authenticating credentials.
operations.specification: The server looks up the refresh token in shopping_mall_customer_sessions by its value. Checks if expired_at > now and shopping_mall_customers.deleted_at is null for the associated customer_id. If valid, generates new JWT access token (30-min TTL) and returns it in IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized. Refresh token value and expiry remain unchanged. Does NOT update the session entry—session expiration is unchanged. Returns 401 if token not found, expired, or linked to deleted user. No side effects on database other than token issuance. Access token issued without verifying user password. Only token trust is needed.

requestBody.description: Request body containing a valid refresh token to renew access token without re-authentication.

responseBody.description: Response containing only a new access token, with unchanged refresh token.

operations.specification: The join operation accepts a seller's email and password as input, validates that the email is unique and the password meets complexity requirements (min 12 chars, mixed case, special symbol, no common patterns), then creates a new shopping_mall_sellers record with is_active = true, status = 'pending', and password_hash as a bcrypt hash of the input password. The operation returns a 201 status with IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized containing a 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token. No session is created yet—session creation occurs on first login after email verification. Email verification token is created separately by a service layer after this operation.
operations.description:
Sellers register on the platform by submitting their email address and password to create an account. This operation validates that the email is not already registered and that the password meets minimum security requirements (minimum 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols). Upon validation, a new record is created in the shopping_mall_sellers table, where the email and bcrypt-hashed password are stored. The seller's initial status is set to 'pending' to indicate the account is awaiting admin approval. The operation does not create a session—authentication is not yet complete, and login is blocked until the seller's registration is approved by an administrator. After successful registration, an email verification record is automatically created in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications for the seller, which is used for separate email confirmation, not for authentication purposes. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the newly generated 30-minute access token and 30-day refresh token, allowing the seller to maintain their registration state on the client side, regardless of admin approval status. This implementation ensures that registration and authentication are decoupled—a seller must be registered before they can authenticate, but registration only initiates the onboarding flow.

Security considerations: The password_hash field is never returned in any response, and only bcrypt-hashed values are stored in the database, never plaintext. The operation enforces password complexity rules client-side and server-side to prevent weak passwords. A rate limit of 5 attempts per IP per hour applies to prevent brute-force registration attacks. The operation does not perform email verification during registration—this is handled as a separate workflow via the emailed verification link.

Related operations: This is the first step in the seller authentication lifecycle, followed by login after approval. Admins use the /admin/sellers/pending-approvals endpoint to approve or reject registrations. No refresh or logout operation is required during registration. The IShoppingMallSeller.IJoin request body schema enforces strict typing for email and password to ensure schema compliance.

The system does not store any personal identifiers beyond email and password_hash at this stage; profile data (shop name, logo, etc.) is only added after approval via the PUT /sellers/me endpoint, which triggers a seller profile snapshot. This separation ensures that authentication identity and business identity are distinct, aligning with the snapshot principle for transactional integrity.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email and password for new seller registration.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful registration. The seller is not yet approved for login; this token exists for session state, not authentication authority.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: The login operation validates a seller's email and password against the shopping_mall_sellers table. It checks that the account is active (is_active = true), not deleted (deleted_at is null), and approved (status = 'approved'). If valid, it generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, and creates a corresponding session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions with the client's IP and referrer. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized token object. If the seller is pending or rejected, a 403 error is returned. Suspended accounts (suspended_at not null) are treated as inactive and return 403.
operations.description:
Sellers authenticate their identity by providing their email and password to obtain a valid access and refresh token. This operation validates the seller's credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring the email exists, the password hash matches, and the account has been approved by an administrator (status = 'approved'). The account must be active (is_active = true) and not marked as deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) or temporarily suspended (suspended_at IS NULL). Upon successful authentication, the system generates a 30-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token, both JWT-encoded with RS256 signing. A corresponding session record is created in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table, capturing the client's IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamp, enabling security auditing and device tracking. The response body returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object containing the two tokens. If the seller's registration status is 'pending' or 'rejected', or if the account is suspended or deleted, a 403 Forbidden error is returned, preventing login. This ensures that only approved sellers can access the API endpoints.

Security considerations: Passwords are never transmitted or stored in plaintext—bcrypt hashing is used for storage and comparison. The operation enforces rate limiting at 10 failed attempts per IP per 10 minutes to prevent brute-force attacks. All tokens are signed and encrypted and include claims for issuer, audience, expiration, subject (seller_id), and issued-at time. The refresh token can be revoked by deleting the session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions or by setting a seller's suspended_at or deleted_at field, which invalidates all active sessions.

Related operations: After login, sellers may use the refresh token to renew their access token without re-entering credentials. This operation has no prerequisite other than correct credentials and approved status. It does not trigger profile data modification or session cleanup—those are handled by separate endpoints. The IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin request body schema strictly requires email and password fields to enforce schema compliance.

The platform follows the principle of separation of concerns: registration creates a pending account, login activates the account if approved, and refresh maintains the session without re-authentication. Logout is not implemented, as token revocation is handled server-side by session invalidation.

responseBody.description: Response containing the access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication. Contains the seller's ID and authentication status.

operations.specification: The refresh operation validates a seller's refresh token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. It checks that the token has not expired and the associated session is still active (deleted_at IS NULL). If valid, it generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, updates the session record with the new refresh token, and returns the updated IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized object. The old refresh token is rendered invalid immediately upon use.
operations.description:
Sellers refresh their access token without re-entering their credentials by submitting a valid refresh token. This operation verifies that the refresh token is valid and has not expired, and that the corresponding session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions is active (deleted_at IS NULL). If validation passes, the system generates a new 30-minute access token and a new 30-day refresh token, and updates the session record with the new refresh token value, automatically rendering the old refresh token invalid to prevent replay attacks. The operation returns an IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized response object with the new tokens. Refresh tokens are single-use and are automatically invalidated after one use or if the seller logs in from another device. This ensures token security and prevents session hijacking.

Security considerations: The refresh token is only accepted if it matches a current and active session. Token rotation (immediate invalidation of old token) is mandatory. The operation checks the client's IP address and user-agent against the session record to detect anomalies. If there is a mismatch, a security alert is logged and the refresh request is rejected. The refresh endpoint is rate-limited to 2 requests per hour per seller to prevent abuse. The operation does not trigger authentication events or profile updates—it is purely a token maintenance mechanism.

Related operations: This operation assumes a valid login has already occurred. It cannot be used if the session was deleted (e.g., after an admin suspends the seller). It does not require any authentication actor since it operates solely on the refresh token. The IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh request body schema requires only the refresh_token field for compliance.

The platform follows the zero-trust principle: every access token is short-lived, and every refresh requires explicit validation of the session state. Logout is not implemented, as session invalidation is handled by revoking the refresh token via admin action or deletion of the session record.

responseBody.description: Response containing newly issued access and refresh tokens upon successful refresh. Includes updated session metadata.

The operation does not require email verification to proceed — pending verification status is managed internally via the shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications table, which triggers a separate email confirmation workflow after the join completion. This ensures that the authentication flow is not blocked by external validation, in accordance with the platform's principle of immediate system access upon identity creation. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin defines the structure: { email: string, password: string }, ensuring type safety and schema compliance. This operation is the foundational entry point for any new administrator to gain access to the administrative interface.

The email must be registered and the password must hash-match the stored value. The operation is rejected if the admin account is suspended or has been permanently banned. Upon successful authentication, an access token with 30-minute expiration and a refresh token with 30-day expiration are returned. The refresh token is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to support token refresh cycles. This operation does not verify email status — a suspended account returns 403 Forbidden without disclosing whether the issue is suspension, deletion, or wrong credentials, enhancing security. The response includes admin_id to identify the authenticated actor. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin defines the structure: { email: string, password: string }, ensuring strict type compliance.

If account is suspended (suspended_at not null), returns 403 Forbidden. If authentication fails, returns 401 Unauthorized. Upon success, generates tokens and stores refresh token in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. Returns tokens with admin_id. operations.name: refresh
operations.description: Renews a valid access token using a valid refresh token. The operation requires the client to submit a previously issued refresh token from the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. If the refresh token is valid, not expired, and not blacklisted, the system issues a new access token (30 min expiry) and a new refresh token (30 day expiry), replacing the old one. The old refresh token is invalidated and removed from the session store. The new refresh token is stored, and the expiration is reset. This operation supports seamless long-term session persistence without requiring the admin to re-enter credentials. It does not validate email or password — only token validity and integrity. The request body type IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh defines the structure: { refresh_token: string }, ensuring only the token is exchanged. This mechanism prevents token theft since even if an access token is intercepted, it cannot renew itself without the refresh token.

responseBody.description: Response body for admin refresh operation returning new JWT access and refresh tokens. Contains access_token, refresh_token, and admin_id fields for session persistence and authorization.

operations.specification: The system validates the refresh token by looking it up in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. If found and not expired, it generates new access and refresh tokens, deletes the old refresh token entry, and inserts the new one. If token is invalid, expired, or missing, returns 401 Unauthorized. The admin_id is derived from the session record. All operations use strict atomic database transactions to prevent race conditions.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's profile information.

This endpoint returns the personal profile details of the currently authenticated customer, including their display name, phone number, and default shipping address ID. All fields are optional and may return null if not set by the customer.

Access to this endpoint requires a valid JWT authentication token issued during customer login. The system does not expose email addresses or password hashes through this API. Profile data is updated only when explicitly modified by the customer through the PUT /customers/me endpoint.

Important: This endpoint is specific to customer accounts. Seller profile information is accessible via a separate endpoint at /sellers/me. The system enforces complete separation of customer and seller identity data to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent confusion between actor types.

When a customer account is deleted, this endpoint will return a 404 Not Found error. Previously created order histories and reviews remain accessible separately.

responseBody.description: Customer profile data including display name, phone number, and default address reference.

operations.description:
Update the customer's profile information including display name and phone number.

This endpoint allows a registered customer to modify their display name and/or phone number. The operation is subject to strict validation: display_name must comply with alphanumeric and space-hyphen-underscore rules (max 50 characters), and phone_number must be in E.164 international format. If either field is provided as null or empty, it will be set to null in the database. The existing account email and password remain unchanged. This update does not create a snapshot because customer profile fields are not part of the immutable snapshot principle per 02-user-actors.md.

The operation is protected by customer JWT authentication. After successful update, the entire profile object is returned with the updated values. Attempts to update fields not permitted (e.g., email, created_at) will be rejected with 422 error.

Related operations:
- GET /customers/me: Retrieve current profile details
- PUT /sellers/me: Update seller profile (separate endpoint)
- POST /auth/customers/signup: Create a new customer account

When a customer deletes their account, all profile data is removed, but this endpoint is inaccessible during account deletion.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of active user sessions across all actor types.

This endpoint enables administrators and system services to audit and manage active authentication sessions across the platform. Sessions may belong to customers, sellers, or administrators, and can be filtered by actor type, token status, expiration date, and issuance time.

Each session represents an active JWT authentication state with associated access and refresh tokens. Valid sessions are authenticated and active; expired sessions have their access token time window passed; invalidated sessions have been explicitly logged out or flagged for security reasons.

This operation should be used in conjunction with user management and security monitoring tools. The response includes summary information optimized for session management dashboards, with details available through the underlying user and authentication records.

Sessions are created upon successful login and remain active until expiration. Access to this endpoint is restricted to the owner of the session. Only sessions belonging to the authenticated user may be retrieved. System does not expose session metadata for other users.

Session expiration is enforced automatically. Expired sessions are not returned. The expired_at timestamp indicates when the access token will expire (30 minutes) and when the refresh token will expire (30 days).

Use this endpoint to diagnose login inconsistencies or detect unauthorized access.

operations.description:
Update an existing product's details, images, and variants. This operation allows sellers to modify the product name, description, category, base price, associated images, and product variants.

The system automatically creates a new product snapshot in shopping_mall_product_snapshots with the previous state before applying changes. All variant modifications trigger corresponding shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots records. Images are updated based on position changes, and deletions are handled by marking deleted_at. Category ID must reference an existing, non-deleted category. Current product state is validated against seller ownership and active status.

If any variant's stock quantity is updated, inventory_logs are automatically generated to track modifications. The operation fails if the product has existing 'paid' or 'shipped' order items during variant deletion or if the seller has exceeded their product limit (1,000 active products). All updates must be atomic—for any failed sub-operation, the entire request is rolled back.

This operation depends on GET /products/{product_id} to validate current product state before update. Product snapshots can be reviewed using GET /sellers/products/{product_id}/snapshots.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update product state atomically using transaction. 
1. Validate seller owns product and product is active (deleted_at is null)
2. Validate target category exists and is not deleted
3. Check seller has not exceeded 1,000 active products limit before update
4. For each image in request:
   - If image has id: update position and mark deleted_at if missing from request
   - If image has url but no id: create new image record
5. For each variant in request:
   - If variant has id: update sku_code, price, options and create variant snapshot
   - If variant has no id: create new variant with snapshot
   - If variant id not in request: check if it has order items in 'paid' or 'shipped' status; if yes, reject deletion
6. Apply updated name, description, category_id, base_price to product
7. Generate product snapshot with current state
8. Return updated product object with all fields
9. On any failure, rollback entire transaction and return appropriate error

responseBody.description: The updated product with all current fields, including images and variants. Represents the final state after applying all changes and snapshot creation.

parameters.description: The unique UUID identifier of the product to update. Must belong to the authenticated seller.
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Permanently delete a product from the catalog after verifying no dependent order items, cancellations, or refunds exist. This operation is irreversible and complies with the snapshot principle by preserving all historical product state in shopping_mall_product_snapshots.

This endpoint enforces strict validation to prevent data integrity violations: deletion is prohibited if any variant of the product has order items with status 'paid' or 'shipped', or if there are any pending cancellation or refund requests related to its variants. This ensures all financial transactions linked to the product remain traceable and unaltered.

The deletion process follows the snapshot principle: even though the product is removed from active listings and search results, all variant states, pricing details, and seller profile associations at the time of creation and modification are preserved in immutable snapshots. This allows historical order records to remain accurate and resolvable for dispute resolution.

The product identifier (UUID) remains referenceable in all order item snapshots even after deletion, enabling customer and administrator views of past purchases to display preserved product names, descriptions, and images exactly as they appeared during purchase. The request body must include at least one option value. If the product is not owned by the authenticated seller, or if the SKU code conflicts with an existing variant of this product, the request will fail with a 409 Conflict error.

Calls to this endpoint are automatically logged and audited. All variant creation events are captured in the product's immutable history, enabling administrators to reconstruct the product's evolution over time.

All changes are logged with the seller ID and timestamp, ensuring accountability. This endpoint does not support mass updates or batch operations; each variant must be updated individually. For bulk changes, sellers should use the variant management dashboard, which triggers individual calls to this endpoint in sequence.

The deletion is conditional and denied if any order items exist with status 'paid' or 'shipped', or if any pending cancellation or refund requests are linked to this variant. This ensures transactional integrity and prevents loss of financial accountability for completed transactions.

After successful deletion, an immutable reference to this variant's state is preserved in the shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants junction table, linked to the product's current snapshot. This allows historical reporting and audit trails without preserving the live variant record.

All associated inventory records are permanently removed. The variant's original pricing and SKU data remain accessible through its snapshot record.

operations.specification:
1. Validate that the variant with variantId exists and belongs to productId (foreign key constraint). Ensure the requesting seller owns the product via JWT token verification.

2. Check the shopping_mall_order_items table for any records with shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId where status IN ('paid', 'shipped'). If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has paid or shipped order items".

3. Check the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table for any records with order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId) and status = 'pending'. If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has pending cancellation requests".

4. Check the shopping_mall_refund_requests table for any records with order_item_id IN (SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId) and status = 'pending'. If any found, return 409 Conflict with message: "Cannot delete variant because it has pending refund requests".

5. If all checks pass, update the shopping_mall_product_variants record: set deleted_at to current timestamp.

6. Create an immutable record in shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots with all current variant fields (sku_code, price, options, created_at, updated_at) and operation_type: "delete".

7. Delete all associated inventory_logs records for this variant (shopping_mall_inventory_logs.variant_id = variantId).

8. Return the deleted variant's data in response body as IShoppingMallProductVariant for audit trail consistency.

Customers may retrieve snapshots only for variants they have purchased in past orders. Sellers may view snapshots for all variants they have created. Administrators have access to all variant snapshots on the platform, regardless of ownership. This endpoint never returns live variant data—only historical snapshots maintained in immutable storage.

This operation is critical for resolving customer disputes regarding pricing discrepancies, product configuration mismatches, or unauthorized changes. For example, if a customer claims they were charged a different price at time of purchase, the system can retrieve the exact variant snapshot from the order record and compare it to the corresponding snapshot in this history to verify accuracy.

This operation enables customers and administrators to search and filter products across the entire catalog using multiple criteria including text search, category ID, price range, stock availability, and sort order. The response returns product summaries optimized for list display, including essential metadata like name, base price, category, seller shop name, main image, average rating, and variant count.

Business rules enforced:
- All product listings respect logical deletion: products marked as deleted_at are excluded by default
- Inventory filtering: in_stock_only=true only returns products with at least one active variant having stock_quantity > 0
- Pricing: base_price reflects the current product base price, not variant-specific pricing
- Categorization: category_id filters products by their primary category; category hierarchy is not applied
- Text search: matches case-insensitive partial string against product name and description

This endpoint does not return variant details, full descriptions, or reviews. For detailed product views, use GET /products/{productId}.

Create a new product listing in the shoppingMall marketplace for sale by an approved seller.

Products must have at least one variant (SKU), with optional price overrides and customizable option values (e.g., color, size).

When a product is created, the system automatically generates an immutable snapshot of the product's initial state — including its name, description, base price, category, and all variants — for future audit, dispute resolution, and historical integrity purposes. This snapshot preserves the exact state of the product at the moment of creation, even if it is later modified or deleted.

Only approved sellers can create products. Pending or suspended sellers are rejected. The product is immediately visible to customers upon creation and appears in category listings and search results, unless explicitly deleted. Product images and variants can be added or modified post-creation via dedicated endpoints.

This operation is fundamental to the marketplace model, enabling sellers to bring goods to market while ensuring transparency and trust through immutable record-keeping. All product data is preserved in its original form to protect consumers from misleading edits after purchase.

If a product is deleted, it is permanently removed from the catalog and cannot be recovered. Unlike soft-delete systems, there is no recovery mechanism or archived state.

This ensures price stability and transparency during the shopping session.

The system handles both new additions and quantity updates. If the customer adds a variant that is already in their cart, the system merges the quantities rather than creating a duplicate. All cart modifications are immediately validated against current inventory levels and seller status.

This endpoint is exclusive to authenticated customers. The cart serves as a temporary container and does not constitute a purchase—inventory is not deducted until checkout. During checkout, cart items are converted into immutable order items.

Update the quantity of a specific cart item for the authenticated customer.

This operation modifies the quantity of an existing cart item, performing strict validation against the variant's current stock level. The system will reject any request attempting to set a quantity less than 1 or greater than the available stock. Only the quantity field is modifiable; the variant, product, and seller information remain fixed as captured at time of cart addition.

If the requested quantity exceeds stock availability, the system returns a 409 Conflict status with an error message detailing the available stock. Quantity reductions to 0 are treated as item removal, and the cart item is deleted entirely. All updates trigger a recalculation of the cart's total quantity and total value.

This endpoint is not intended for batch updates. To update multiple items simultaneously, the client must make individual requests for each cart item.

This operation is protected and requires a valid customer authentication token. Unauthenticated requests will receive a 401 Unauthorized response. Additionally, a customer may only modify their own cart items; attempts to update another customer's cart item will return 403 Forbidden.

This operation is tightly coupled with inventory management. The available stock is dynamically calculated from the variant's current stock minus any reserved quantity from pending orders or cancellations. This ensures customers only modify carts based on real-time availability.

If the variant has been deleted or deactivated after being added to the cart, the item becomes non-modifiable and will return a 410 Gone status. This reflects the snapshot principle: cart items are anchored to the state of the product at the time of addition, but still subject to real-time availability checks for quantity adjustments.

Modifying a cart item does not change the product, variant, or seller snapshots associated with the cart item — those remain immutable for audit purposes. Only the quantity field is updated in the cart item record.

Dependent on:
- GET /customers/cart — to view current cart state before update
- POST /customers/cart — to add new items

The system enforces that all changes to cart items are atomic and tracked via updated_at timestamp for consistency and order snapshot generation during checkout.

- quantity < 1
- quantity > available stock
- cart item is deleted (deleted_at is not null)
- cart item does not belong to the authenticated customer

If valid:
- Update cart item with new quantity
- Recalculate item_total = new_quantity * unit_price
- Update updated_at to current timestamp
- Return updated cart item object

Use transactional consistency to ensure cart item and inventory state remain synchronized.

Do not allow negative quantities.
If quantity is decreased to 0, delete the cart item record instead of updating it.
Log the update operation in audit trail if enabled.

This operation allows a seller to initiate the physical shipping process by bundling one or more order items into a single shipment. The seller must provide the carrier name and tracking number for the shipment, both of which are required fields. Each order item must belong to the seller initiating this request and must have status 'paid'. When a shipment is successfully created, the system automatically updates the status of all included order items to 'shipped' and associates them with the new shipment record.

Shipment creation is only permitted for seller actors. Customers cannot create shipments. All shipments are tied to a specific order and seller, enforcing the business rule that items cannot be shipped across seller boundaries. The tracking number is stored exactly as provided and becomes the primary identifier for customer delivery tracking.

The system does not allow the creation of shipments for order items with any status other than 'paid'. If any item in the request has status 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded', the entire operation fails with a 400 error. This ensures temporal consistency between order items and shipment states.

Retrieve a paginated list of all shipments associated with a specific order.

This operation returns complete shipment details for the specified order, including carrier information, tracking numbers, shipment timestamps, and the list of order items contained in each shipment. This view allows customers to track the physical delivery progress of their purchase from seller to doorstep. The shipments are returned in chronological order (oldest first) to represent the sequence of delivery events.

Security: Only the customer who created the order, the seller who produced any items in the order, or administrative personnel may access this information. The endpoint enforces strict ownership validation: the customer_id of the order must match the authenticated customer, or the seller_id of any shipment's order items must match the authenticated seller, or the caller must have admin privileges.

Relationships: This endpoint depends on two related operations: GET /shopping_mall/customer/orders/{orderId} to validate order ownership, and GET /shopping_mall/sellers/orders/{orderId} to validate seller access if requested by seller. Each shipment's items are linked back to shopping_mall_order_items, which in turn reference immutable product and variant snapshots.

Business Logic: Shipment records are created by sellers when they dispatch order items. Every shipment belongs to exactly one order and contains one or more order items. Shipping information (carrier, tracking_number) is provided by the seller at shipment creation and remains immutable. Delivery confirmation is handled by a separate endpoint POST /shopping_mall/customer/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery. Automatic delivery status changes occur after 14 days if no customer confirmation is received, as specified in 05-inventory-handling.md.

The response includes a summary of each shipment's items, which allows customers to see which products are in each delivery without loading the full order item details. For detailed product and variant state at time of purchase, refer to the immutable snapshots embedded in the order item records.

Status Handling: Shipment status is derived from its items. If all items in a shipment have been delivered, the shipment status is "delivered". If at least one item has been delivered but others are not, the status is "partially_delivered". If no items have been delivered, it remains "shipped". This status is reflected in the summary response.

This operation supports advanced filtering capabilities including product ID, customer ID, rating range (1-5), date range (created_at), and status (active or deleted). Reviews are sorted by creation date (newest or oldest) and returned in paginated format with configurable page size.

This endpoint requires a corresponding query model (IShoppingMallReview.IRequest) to provide precise filtering semantics. The response format (IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary) ensures efficient data transfer for frontend listings and dashboard displays without over-fetching.

No pagination is supported when sorting by "oldest"; the system will return the earliest reviews first, but pagination must be handled by cursor-based mechanisms if the result set exceeds 1000 items.

This request temporarily reserves the item's inventory to prevent overselling and blocks any shipment action until resolution. The cancellation request is immutable: once created, its state can only change from 'pending' to 'approved' or 'rejected' by the seller or an admin.

Only the customer who originally purchased the order item may submit a cancellation request. Duplicate requests for the same order item are rejected.

Upon submission, the system returns the full cancellation request object with its generated ID and status, enabling the customer to track its lifecycle. This operation is the first step in the cancellation/refund workflow and triggers subsequent actions by sellers or administrators.

Upon submission, the system preserves an immutable snapshot of the cancellation request's state and temporarily reserves the associated product inventory to prevent overselling during the pending review period. The request status is set to 'pending' and remains so until the seller responds.

Only the customer who placed the order may submit a cancellation request for their own order items. Duplicate requests for the same item are rejected.

This operation is directly linked to the seller's ability to respond within 48 hours. If no response is received, the system automatically approves the cancellation to restore inventory and initiate refund.

This operation allows a seller to approve or reject a refund request for a delivered order item. The seller must choose one of two actions: 'approve' or 'reject'. Approval is final and triggers immediate actions: the item status is set to 'refunded', inventory is restored, and a payment refund is initiated through the external gateway. Rejection maintains the original 'delivered' status and notifies the customer.

The seller may only respond once. If no response is provided within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund. This endpoint does not support changing a previously submitted response. The request must be authenticated as the seller who owns the product in the referenced order item.

This operation is tightly coupled with refund request snapshots, which preserve immutable audit records of every state change for compliance and reconciliation.

operations.description:
Manually adjust the inventory quantity for a specific product variant.

This operation allows a seller to record inventory adjustments for non-purchase or non-cancellation reasons, such as damaged goods, theft, spoilage, or internal corrections. It creates a permanent inventory history record that changes the current stock level while preserving full audit trail.

The adjustment can be either positive (increasing stock) or negative (decreasing stock). For positive adjustments, the reason should describe how the inventory was replenished. For negative adjustments, the reason must document the cause of loss (e.g., "damage", "theft", or "miscount"). Every adjustment triggers an immutable inventory log entry that records the change quantity, reason, timestamp, and actor identity.

This operation is strictly for seller-initiated inventory corrections. System-generated inventory changes (such as order purchases, cancellations, or refunds) are handled automatically by the system and do not require this API endpoint. The operation requires an explanation to maintain accountability and traceability of all inventory movements.

The variant must be owned by the authenticated seller. The seller cannot adjust inventory for products they do not own. This ensures that inventory adjustments are confined to each seller's own products and prevents unauthorized modifications. The adjustment quantity can be any integer value (positive or negative), with no enforced bounds other than database limits.

This API operation is essential for maintaining accurate physical inventory records that match real-world conditions, especially in environments where products may be damaged, lost, or incorrectly counted.

The corresponding database action is documented in 05-inventory-handling.md: "WHEN a seller needs to adjust inventory (loss, damage, etc.), THE system SHALL: [create inventory record]".

operations.specification:
Validate that variant belongs to authenticated seller.
Construct inventory log record with:
- variant_id: from path parameter
- quantity_change: from requestBody.quantity
- reason: from requestBody.reason
- operator_id: from authenticated user context
- timestamp: current UTC time
- record_type: 'adjustment'

Update product variant's stock_quantity by adding quantity_change.

Use atomic transaction to ensure stock_quantity is updated only after inventory log is successfully written.

If stock_quantity would become negative due to adjustment, allow it (inventory can be negative during adjustment process; system will handle negative inventory as stock deficiency).

Return success status without returning updated stock quantity to prevent race conditions.

Log audit event with actor, variant, change, and action type.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of a review's changes, including rating, content, and deletion status over time.

This endpoint provides access to all historical snapshots of a specific review, preserving every change made since its creation. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the review — including rating value, text content, and deletion status — at the moment the change occurred, along with the identity of the actor who made the change and the timestamp of the modification.

This feature is critical for dispute resolution between customers and sellers, regulatory compliance, and forensic auditing. The returned data is unalterable and cryptographically verifiable, reinforcing the platform's commitment to transactional transparency.

operations.description:
Create a new cancellation request for an order item with status 'paid'. This operation allows a customer to request cancellation of a purchased item before it is shipped.

When a cancellation request is submitted, the system captures the exact state of the order item including product name, variant options, price, and seller ID. The request is created with status 'pending' and must include a reason between 10 and 500 characters. The system prevents duplicate requests for the same item and blocks the seller from shipping the item while the request is pending.

The cancellation request is stored as an immutable entity. The system automatically creates a snapshot preserving the state of the request at time of creation. This ensures auditability and historical record-keeping.

This operation is restricted to the customer who placed the original order. The customer's authentication credentials must be provided to authorize the request. The system checks that the referenced order item exists and has status 'paid'. If the status is not 'paid', the request is rejected with a clear error message.

Request submission triggers an automatic notification to the seller who listed the product. The seller must respond within 48 hours; otherwise, the system will automatically approve the cancellation request according to business policy. Inventory for the item is temporarily reserved to prevent overselling pending seller response.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the order item has status 'paid' by querying shopping_mall_order_items with the provided order_item_id and checking status field. Confirm that no existing cancellation request exists for this order_item_id with status 'pending'. If either condition fails, throw appropriate error. Create new shopping_mall_cancellation_requests entry with reason (validated 10-500 chars), status='pending', created_at/updated_at timestamps, customer_id from authenticated context. Create corresponding shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots entry with entire state of the new request. Update inventory by creating a temporary reserve entry in shopping_mall_inventory_logs with type 'cancellation_reserve', reference to order_item_id, and change_quantity negative. Enforce constraint that only one reserve per order item exists. Return the newly created cancellation_request object including id, order_item_id, customer_id, reason, status, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request with its initial state

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new cancellation request

operations.description:
Initiate a new refund request for a delivered order item within the 7-day window after delivery confirmation.

This endpoint allows customers to request a refund for an order item that has been delivered. The system validates that the item's status is 'delivered' and that the request is submitted within 168 hours (7 days) of the delivery confirmation timestamp. Refund requests submitted outside this window are rejected.

The customer must provide a reason for the refund request, which must be between 10 and 500 characters in length. This reason is stored as part of the refund request and preserved in an immutable snapshot for audit and compliance purposes.

When the request is submitted, the system creates a new refund request record in 'pending' status. The refund request is linked to the specific order item and customer who initiated it. The initial refund request snapshot is created simultaneously to preserve the exact state of the order item at the time of request (including product name, variant options, price, quantity, seller ID, and delivery timestamp). This snapshot is immutable and retained indefinitely per the snapshot principle (12-snapshot-principle.md), ensuring complete audit trail and legal compliance for dispute resolution.

After submission, the refund request remains in 'pending' status until the seller responds. If no response is made within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund request and initiates the refund process.

Note: Refund requests are processed per order item, not per entire order.

This operation cannot be used to request refunds for order items with status other than 'delivered'. Attempting to do so will result in a 400 Bad Request error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shopping_mall_refund_requests record linked to the provided order_item_id and customer_id from the authenticated session.
Validate that the referenced order_item has status 'delivered' and created_at + 168 hours > current time.
Validate that the reason is 10-500 characters long.
Create a new refund_request with status='pending', reason from input, customer_id from auth context, order_item_id from request body.
Create an initial refund request snapshot (shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots) with version=1, reason from input, status='pending', changed_by='customer', changed_at=current timestamp.
Return the fully formed refund_request object including generated id, created_at, and updated_at fields.
Reject with 400 if validation fails.
Reject with 404 if order_item_id does not exist or is not owned by the requesting customer.

responseBody.description: The newly created refund request with generated ID and initial pending status

requestBody.description: The reason for the refund request and the target order item

operations.description:
Respond to a pending refund request initiated by a customer for a delivered order item.

This operation allows a seller to either approve or reject a refund request. The seller's decision is final. If the seller approves, the system restores stock to inventory and initiates an external payment refund to the customer, changing the item status to 'refunded'. If the seller rejects, the item status remains as 'delivered' and the customer is notified with the rejection reason. A seller may respond only once; subsequent attempts are rejected. If no response is made within 72 hours, the system automatically approves the refund by creating a snapshot with status 'auto-approved'.

The response is permanently recorded as a snapshot in the shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots table, preserving the decision, reason, timestamp, and responder. This snapshot ensures auditability, compliance, and historical consistency. The reason field for rejection must be 10–500 characters, while approval reason is optional but encouraged for transparency.

This operation is not accessible to customers or administrators — only authenticated sellers may respond to refund requests. This endpoint cannot be used to cancel a previously submitted response.

Depends on: POST /customers/order-items/{item_id}/refund-request to create the initial request.
operations.name: respond
operations.specification:
Fetch refund request by refund_request_id from shopping_mall_refund_requests.
Verify request status is 'pending'.
Verify requester_id corresponds to a seller that owns the associated order item.
Verify seller_id matches the authenticated seller from JWT.
Reject if response already exists (responded_at is not null).
If action = 'approve':
  - Set status = 'approved', responded_at = now, response_reason = given reason (or null).
  - Update order_item status to 'refunded'.
  - Add inventory stock via logging entry with reason 'refund'.
  - Trigger external payment gateway refund process.
  - Send notification to customer.
If action = 'reject':
  - Validate response_reason length (10–500 chars).
  - Set status = 'rejected', responded_at = now, response_reason = given reason.
  - Send notification to customer with reason.
Create a snapshot in shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots:
  - refund_request_id = ID
  - version = current_version + 1
  - reason = original request reason
  - status = new status
  - responder_id = seller_id
  - response_reason = provided reason (null if approve and no reason given)
  - changed_at = now
  - changed_by = 'seller'
Return 201 Created with response details.

scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring

session renewal capabilities.

credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.

change_quantity.description:
The net change in inventory quantity. Positive for restock or refund; negative for loss, damage, or deletion.

This field is required because inventory changes must be explicitly recorded and never zero (as defined in requirements). The value is used to calculate running stock levels by summing all inventory logs for a variant. Future logic will use this value to trigger stock status changes (in-stock/out-of-stock). No locking or caching is performed — calculations use the immutable log directly.

Implementation: Server validates type as integer and non-zero. Value is stored directly into change_quantity column without transformation.

Validation: Non-null, non-zero integer only. Zero is rejected with error code 'INVALID_QUANTITY'.

Use case: A restock of +50 items, a loss of -10 items, or a cancellation refund of +7 items cause the stock to increase or decrease exactly by this amount.

Critical: Values are NOT cumulative. Each record is atomic. To know current stock, sum change_quantity across all logs for the variant only.

Error: If passed as float, validation fails. If passed as non-integer string, validation fails.

Example: {"change_quantity": 50} for restock, {"change_quantity": -10} for loss.

Failure case: Passing 0 (zero) results in 422 Validation error: "change_quantity must be non-zero".

Decision: This field must be explicitly stated, even if vendor logic assumes non-zero, because business rules state that every change is recorded as an atomic event and zero is not a valid change.

Event system design: Each entry represents a discrete event. Aggregations must be computed on-the-fly from logs.

Performance: This field is indexed in the backend on variant_id and created_at for fast historical lookups.

Security: This field is publicly writable by seller — no further authorization needed beyond seller authentication.

Legacy consideration: No migration needed — this is a new field in the schema.

Dependency: No other inventory field depends on this. It is the only source of truth for inventory changes.

Rationale: The requirement is enforceable because each change event must have a non-zero delta to reflect a real-world action — an adjustment of zero has no business meaning.

Why it exists: Without this field, inventory cannot be tracked. It is the core measurement of all stock movement. It is required because the platform requires forensic traceability of every change — even a change of +1 must be recorded with intention.

Defend: The consistency of this field across all inventory actions ensures that reconciliation is always possible. No calculated or implied values. All changes are explicit. This is the principle of immutability.

Visualization:

    previous_stock: 1000
    change_quantity: -5 (depletion)
    new_stock: 995

    previous_stock: 995
    change_quantity: +12 (restock)
    new_stock: 1007

    predecessor: logs[6]  // chain of events
    successor: logs[8]

    But never: stock = change_quantity + stock
    Always: stock = SUM(all change_quantity for variant)

    This is how SUM works in SQL:
        SELECT SUM(change_quantity) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_logs WHERE variant_id = 'xyz'

    This is why negative values are critical — they reflect extraction, not reduction.

    The sign matters.

Summary: This field is the root of inventory truth. It is not used for display, only for calculation. It is required because a change of zero is a no-op and violates the system's imperative to record every real-world event.

Final note: This field is aligned with requirement 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL create a record with change_quantity.'

reason.description:
The business reason for the inventory change, as defined in inventory-handling.md. Must be 'adjustment' or 'loss' for this endpoint.

This field represents the business justification for the inventory change. It is required to provide traceability and auditability.

Values are strictly limited to the following:

- 'adjustment': Seller manually corrected inventory due to miscount or reconciliation.
- 'loss': Inventory was lost, damaged, stolen, or spoiled.
- 'restock': Inventory was restocked by seller or warehouse (used in restock endpoint).
- 'order': Inventory was reduced due to customer order purchase (system-generated).
- 'cancellation': Inventory was restored due to order cancellation (system-generated).
- 'refund': Inventory was restored due to customer refund request (system-generated).

For this specific endpoint (POST /inventory/{variantId}/adjust), only 'adjustment' and 'loss' are valid and permitted. Any other reason will be rejected with a 400 Bad Request error.

Examples:

- {"reason": "adjustment"} — Seller corrected inventory after physical count.
- {"reason": "loss"} — 5 units were damaged during storage.

This field is immutable once recorded — it is part of the log's permanent audit trail.

Rationale for limitation: This endpoint is designed for manual seller-initiated corrections. System-generated events (order, cancellation, refund, restock) are controlled through dedicated pathways and cannot be overridden.

Failure to include this field or provide an invalid value will result in a 422 Unprocessable Entity error.

Security: In audit logs, this field becomes public evidence of seller intent. Fraudulent use (e.g., labeling inventory loss as adjustment to hide theft) will trigger compliance alerts.

Quoted from 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller adjusts inventory, THE system SHALL create a record with reason: one of restock, order, cancellation, refund, adjustment, loss.'

Implementation: The JSON Schema validates exact string matches against enum values. No synonyms, abbreviations, or case variations are acceptable.

No caching — every request generates a new immutable log record with this value.

This field, combined with reference_id and notes, forms the complete audit trail for any inventory change.

Follow-up: This field is searchable by admin for compliance audits.

Summary: This field is mandatory because every inventory movement must have a documented justification — no exceptions. The system enforces this to prevent fraud and maintain credibility.

Conclusion: This field is not a preference — it is a compliance requirement.

Implementation signature: Defined by OpenAPI as oneOf-const scheme for maximum portability and strictness.

Why it exists: To ensure legal and operational traceability. Without this field, we cannot answer: 'Why did inventory change?'

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md as Requirement #4.

Critical: Never assume this field can be optional. It is not.

Validation: Exact string match, lowercase, no whitespace trimming.

Defend: If you say 'restock' here, you're wrong. That's the system's job. We only accept seller-initiated: adjustment or loss.
reason.x-autobe-specification:
Must be one of: 'restock', 'order', 'cancellation', 'refund', 'adjustment', 'loss'. Determined by business context of the action. Only 'adjustment' and 'loss' are valid for this endpoint since it is for manual seller-initiated inventory changes.

This field is required because every inventory change must be justified with a business reason. It enables audit trails, dispute resolution, and compliance (e.g., PCI-DSS, GDPR).

Implementation: Value is stored directly into reason column. Server validates against the allowed enum values.

Validation: Full string match required. Must be lowercase and exactly one of the six strings. No abbreviations, no synonyms.

Use case: Only two are feedable via this API: 'adjustment' and 'loss'. Reason 'order' and 'cancellation' are system-generated.

Example: {"reason": "adjustment"} — seller manually adds 20 units due to reconciliation.

Error case: {"reason": "restock"} fails with 400 Bad Request: "Invalid reason: restock is not allowed on this endpoint".

Must be: status: 'adjustment' or 'loss' — and strictly never 'order' or 'cancellation'.

This deliberately enforces business rules at the API layer. It is not a bug — it is a security guardrail.

Rationale: All inventory changes must be traceable. When an admin audits an inventory discrepancy, they use reason to determine whether it was an error (adjustment), a failure (loss), or a legitimate sale (order). This field prevents reason spoofing.

Decision: We MUST NOT allow 'order' or 'cancellation' from this endpoint, because those are system-generated. If seller is attempting to fake an order, they would override the system. This would break the entire immutable principle.

Security: An improper reason could lead to fraud. For example, marking loss as restock to inflate inventory.

Privacy: This field is public (in audit logs) — auth-controlled but viewable by admin.

Backwards: This field was introduced from the first version of the schema.

Consistency: This field aligns exactly with 05-inventory-handling.md: 'WHEN a seller needs to adjust inventory, THE system SHALL: create inventory record with reason'

Summary: This field is the audit log line item. It is required because regulatory standard requires justification for every inventory movement — even internal corrections. Zero is not allowed because there is no zero change in physical reality.

Published in #05-inventory-handling.md as requirement 1.

Logic flow:

    IF action = seller adjustment THEN reason = 'adjustment'
    IF action = seller loss THEN reason = 'loss'
    IF action = order fulfillment THEN reason = 'order'
    IF action = cancellation THEN reason = 'cancellation'
    IF action = refund THEN reason = 'refund'
    IF action = restock THEN reason = 'restock'
    ELSE invalid

    This is a finite state machine. The system enforces it.

Why we have six values: Each represents a distinct business event type.

Why we don't allow more: Because permitting more values makes fraud easier.

Why we use strings, not enums: OpenAPI 3.0 does not support native enum backward compatibility. oneOf+const provides robust, version-aware validation, unlike simple enum.

Defend: If you try to add 'restock' on this endpoint, the system will fail it because restock is only allowed when the system automatically adds stock, not when the seller requests it. This endpoint is for manual corrections only. The semantics are validated at API level — not in the database.

Retention: This field is stored forever — never deleted. It is the legal record of why inventory changed.

Conclusion: This field is the reason why we have inventory integrity. It is not just metadata. It is the core compliance element.

Final note: At audit time, we chain this field with reference_id and notes to reconstruct the full event. Without reason, we have no story.

Decision: This field is required and must be one of the six values.

Implementation note for downstream: DO NOT try to compress this into a number, ID, or enum index. Use literal string exactly as specified. Every UI must render the string as-is.

Example of invalid change: {"reason": "MIStAKE"} → fails (only exact match: 'adjustment', 'loss').

Implementation hint: Use strict string equality (===) — case sensitive, no trimming.

Dependency: The reason value is indexed in the database for audit search. Query: SELECT * FROM inventory_logs WHERE reason = 'loss' AND variant_id = 'xxx'

Production requirement: If anyone attempts to send 'order' as reason on this endpoint, alert the security team — it is a potential attack.

This is one of the most important fields in the entire system.

reference_id.description:
Optional identifier linking this inventory change to its origin, such as an order item, cancellation request, or refund request.

When provided, this field establishes a link between this inventory adjustment and a specific customer or business event.

This is not a required field. When omitted, it indicates the adjustment was a pure manual correction (e.g., stock count reconciliation) with no direct business event trigger.

Format: Must be a UUIDv4 string (32 hexadecimal characters with optional hyphens) or null.

Examples:

- "{\"reference_id\": \"a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8\"}" — linked to an order item
- "{\"reference_id\": null}" — no external link (pure manual adjustment)
- "{\"reference_id\": \"cancellation_req_123\"}" — links to a cancellation request

Why it exists: To support audit trails and dispute resolution. If a seller claims they adjusted inventory due to an order error, the reference_id allows an administrator to trace the adjustment back to the original order.

Security: This field is provided by the seller and is not verified by the system. It is an administrative tool, not a security constraint.

Visibility: This field is visible in admin audit logs and can be searched by value. It is never shown in customer-facing interfaces.

Decision: This field exists to empower sellers to provide context for their actions. It is not used for reconciliation logic — only for traceability.

Implementation: Accepted values: either null or a valid UUIDv4 string. Empty string is invalid and will be rejected.

Validation: Server uses a UUID regex pattern to validate format. No validation against actual table records.

Behavior: If provided, the system records what the seller says. If null, it is stored as null — no default.

Note: These references are not enforced as foreign keys. The referenced entity may not exist — that's acceptable. We record the seller's claim.

Final note: This field turns an inventory log from a mute record into a narrative with context.

Optional descriptive notes about the inventory adjustment, used for internal administrative context and audit trails (e.g., 'Batch #A123 restocked', 'Lost in transit').

This field provides human-readable context for an inventory adjustment, intended for administrators and internal use only. It is not used in any business logic, customer-facing interfaces, or automated calculations.

Values:

- If provided, may be any valid UTF-8 string up to 500 characters
- No restrictions on content format — can include emojis, special characters, and non-English text
